title: Power Steering — How EPAS Helps
introduction: Electronic power assist steering, or EPAS, uses an electric motor to reduce the effort needed to steer. I picture it as a helping hand on the steering mechanism: you supply the steering input, and the system supplies assistance. This overview explains that relationship; it is not a fault-finding or repair procedure.

edits.text: The EPAS system responds to your steering-wheel inputs and uses an electric motor to provide steering assistance. You still turn the wheel; the motor reduces the effort required. The electronic controller adjusts that help according to steering effort and operating conditions, providing more assistance at low speed and less at higher speed to preserve road feel.
edits.why: Steering input and steering assistance have different jobs. This distinction explains how the driver remains in control while the motor helps, and why assistance can feel different as vehicle speed changes.
